summary: Iteration 10 - Chart runtime kustomisasi (span + start time) for Trend real-time & History Trend widgets. Frontend-only Playwright end-to-end on published Demo 'ghdhbuxrp4e' (Utama has trend, Laporan has history). All gear buttons, panels, inputs, validation, apply, persistence (localStorage scada-chart:<base>:<widgetId>), reset, arrows, NOW behaved exactly as specified. No regressions.
critical_code_review_comments: ChartSettings.jsx line 28: `maxMs / SPAN_MS.day` in the error message hardcodes 'hari' regardless of chosen unit. Fine because the constraint is currently only used by Trend with maxMs=7d, but if reused for min/hour caps the message would confuse users.

ChartSettings.jsx line 6 toLocalInput uses `new Date(ms - tz)` which is standard but may be off during DST transitions; consider `new Date(ms).toLocaleString('sv-SE').slice(0,16).replace(' ','T')` for safety.

DataWidgets.jsx line 50 (Trend): when user sets custom span, `win = span_value * SPAN_MS[unit]` is used for both the initial `/history` fetch (minutes = ceil(win/60000)) and the live-tail window filter. For very small spans (<1 min) the ceil rounds up to 1 min which is minor. OK.

DataWidgets.jsx HistoryTrend uses one useChartPrefs entry that stores span AND start together; toggling Latest ↔ custom is persisted, which is desired. Note: start is an absolute epoch, so a saved custom date will remain 'stuck in the past' after reload even weeks later — arguably intended per requirements but could surprise operators.

ChartSettings prevents apply when custom start is chosen but datetime is empty. Good. However, if the user picks 'Tanggal & jam' then leaves default `Date.now() - span`, no explicit error is thrown even though the seed value may be misleading; acceptable.

No max sanity check on History Trend span (only Trend limits to 7 days). Requesting e.g. 365 days will send a wide samples query; backend has limit=20000 which caps rows but the API call itself is unrestricted. Consider soft cap or warning.
